name: Southern Magnolia
water: Deeply every 1-2 weeks (once established, they are quite drought-tolerant).
description: An iconic evergreen tree of the South, famous for its large, waxy green leaves and massive, fragrant white blossoms that bloom in late spring.

name: Oakleaf Hydrangea
light: Partial Shade (needs protection from the harsh afternoon Southern sun).
water: Consistently moist; requires frequent watering during summer heat waves.
description: A native shrub with leaves shaped like those of an oak tree. It produces beautiful cone-shaped white flower clusters that fade to a dusty pink as they age.

name: Gulf Coast Muhly Grass
water: Low; very drought-tolerant once the root system is established.
description: Often called "Pink Muhly Grass," this ornamental grass is famous for the airy, cotton-candy pink clouds of flowers that appear in late fall, creating a stunning landscape effect.

name: Spanish Bayonet
water: Very Low; only needs occasional watering during extreme dry spells.
description: A striking, structural plant with stiff, evergreen leaves that end in a sharp "bayonet" point. It produces tall spikes of bell-shaped white flowers in the summer.

name: American Beautyberry
water: Moderate; prefers regular moisture but can handle dry spells once mature.
description: deciduous shrub best known for its spectacular, tightly-packed clusters of neon-purple berries that wrap around the stems in the autumn, providing food for local birds.
